nx_bcc_001: Cane mechanics: hold the cane on the STRONG side and advance it with the weak leg - the cane widens the base toward strength. Options placing it on the weak side reverse the physics.
nx_bcc_002: Stairs with crutches: up with the good, down with the bad - the strong leg does the lifting, so it leads up while crutches stay with the injured leg.
nx_bcc_003: Stage the wound from the description before reading options: shallow, open, red-pink moist bed without slough is stage 2 - depth and tissue type decide the stage, not size.
nx_bcc_004: Heel protection has a best answer: float the heels completely off the bed with pillows under the calves. Donut cushions and massage of bony areas are classic planted errors.
nx_bcc_005: 'Just inserted' plus 'before first use' is the X-ray question - radiographic confirmation is the only initial verification. pH and auscultation options are for ongoing checks or are outdated.
nx_bcc_006: Clear liquids are see-through at room temperature: broth, gelatin, clear juices, black coffee, tea. Anything opaque - milk, cream soup, orange juice with pulp - is full liquid or beyond.
nx_bcc_007: Renal-diet selections limit potassium, sodium, phosphorus and fluid: the correct tray avoids high-potassium fruits, processed meats and dairy loads. Scan each option for the hidden potassium bomb.
nx_bcc_008: Aspiration-precaution SATA: upright 90 degrees for meals and 30-plus minutes after, chin tuck, slow small bites, no straws if directed, suction available - reject anything supine or hurried.
nx_case_cauti_001_q1: In the recognize-cues phase, hunt the modifiable risk sitting in plain sight: an indwelling catheter without a current indication is the classic one - question the device before anything else.
nx_case_cauti_001_q2: New confusion in an older adult with a catheter is the pivot cue: in this population, mental-status change often IS the infection presentation - flag it as significant, not as baseline aging.
nx_case_cauti_001_q3: Analyze-cues questions ask you to name the pattern: fever source plus device plus new confusion clusters as catheter-associated UTI progressing toward urosepsis - choose the interpretation covering ALL findings.
nx_case_cauti_001_q4: For suspected urosepsis, sequence matters inside the SATA: cultures BEFORE antibiotics, fluids, and catheter removal or exchange - accept options honoring that order, reject antibiotics-first.
nx_case_cauti_001_q5: Delegation inside a deteriorating-client case: assistive personnel take stable, measurable tasks (recording intake and output, vital signs at stated intervals) - never assessment, titration, or evaluation.
nx_case_cauti_001_q6: Evaluate-outcomes questions want the finding that proves the INTERVENTION worked: clearing mentation and stabilising vitals show perfusion restored - a single improved number with worsening mentation does not.
nx_case_hemorrhage_001_q1: Recognize the early-shock cluster: restlessness, thirst and rising pulse with still-normal blood pressure. Compensation hides volume loss - the cue set matters more than any single value.
nx_case_hemorrhage_001_q2: Trend questions grade pattern recognition: rising HR with narrowing pressure after surgery reads as compensated hypovolemia - pick the hypothesis that explains the trajectory, not a snapshot.
nx_case_hemorrhage_001_q3: When compensation breaks (BP falling, refill 4 s, oliguria), prioritise perfusion: the falling urine output is the organ-level evidence that makes this decompensated shock.
nx_case_hemorrhage_001_q4: Hemorrhage order sets: isotonic crystalloid bolus, type and crossmatch, serial CBC, keep NPO for possible return to OR - accept the volume-and-prepare options, reject anything that delays fluids.
nx_case_hemorrhage_001_q5: Positioning for hypotension: supine with legs elevated (modified Trendelenburg per protocol) - options raising the head of bed work against cerebral perfusion.
nx_case_hemorrhage_001_q6: Treatment success in hypovolemia is measured at the kidney and the pulse: urine output recovering with heart rate falling toward baseline - reassurance statements and warm skin alone do not prove volume restored.
nx_case_opioid_001_q1: RR 8 and shallow on opioids is respiratory depression: the recognize-cues answer pairs the rate with sedation level - deep snoring here is an airway warning, not comfortable sleep.
nx_case_opioid_001_q2: Risk-factor questions want the potentiator: obstructive sleep apnea (or concurrent sedatives) multiplies opioid respiratory risk - pick the history element that changes drug handling or airway tone.
nx_case_opioid_001_q3: First action for opioid-induced hypoventilation: stimulate and support - arouse the client, position the airway, apply oxygen - while preparing reversal; do-first questions grade the airway reflex.
nx_case_opioid_001_q4: After naloxone works, the tested fact is its short half-life: renarcotization is the risk, so continued close monitoring is the answer - 'episode resolved' options are the trap.
nx_case_opioid_001_q5: Post-event plan SATA: continuous or scheduled respiratory monitoring, sedation scale, hold-and-notify parameters, naloxone available - reject options that resume the prior regimen unchanged.
nx_case_opioid_001_q6: Evaluate the NEW regimen against both goals at once: adequate analgesia AND respiratory safety - the best finding shows pain controlled with normal rate and alertness, not one without the other.
nx_hpm_001: Six-month milestones: sits with support moving to independent, rolls both ways, transfers objects hand to hand, babbles. Options describing pulling to stand or pincer grasp belong to older infants.
nx_hpm_002: Choking-prevention questions target round, firm, slippery foods: whole grapes, hot dogs, nuts, hard candy. The eliminated food is the one matching that shape profile.
nx_hpm_003: MMR is live: pregnancy and significant immunosuppression are the contraindications. Screen options for those two states - mild illness and family history are decoys.
nx_hpm_004: Folic acid's why is neural tube closure in the first weeks - before pregnancy is recognised - which is exactly why supplementation starts preconception.
nx_hpm_005: Boggy fundus displaced laterally reads as a full bladder: have the client void, then massage and reassess - the displacement is the clue that separates this from simple atony.
nx_hpm_006: Newborn findings sort by system consequence: central cyanosis, marked respiratory signs, or temperature instability need action now; acrocyanosis and molding are normal-variation decoys.
nx_hpm_007: Recurrent late decelerations on oxytocin: stop the infusion first, then reposition, oxygen per protocol, and notify - the drug driving uteroplacental insufficiency is the modifiable cause.
nx_hpm_008: Erikson by stage: adolescence is identity versus role confusion. Match the stage to its named conflict and ignore options quoting neighbouring stages.
nx_hpm_009: 'NOT normal aging' questions hide one disease finding among expected changes: confusion, depression and incontinence are never normal aging - presbyopia, slower reflexes and shorter sleep are.
nx_hpm_010: Normal-aging SATA: accept sensory decline (presbyopia, presbycusis), decreased skin elasticity, slower reaction time; reject anything cognitive (confusion) or functional (incontinence) - those signal pathology.
nx_moc_001: Assess-first questions rank by ABC plus acuity of change: the client with a new or unstable airway/breathing/circulation problem beats chronic or expected findings every time.
nx_moc_002: Delegation to AP: stable client, routine task, predictable outcome - hygiene, ambulation, vitals on stable clients, I&O. Assessment, teaching and evaluation words disqualify an option instantly.
nx_moc_003: LPN scope sits between: reinforcing teaching, routine medications, focused data collection on stable clients - not initial assessment, care planning, IV push meds, or unstable clients.
nx_moc_004: Detailed procedure-risk questions belong to the surgeon: the nurse's role is to contact the provider and witness the signature, not to explain operative risks - answering them is practicing outside scope.
nx_moc_005: A withdrawn consent stands even after signing: stop preparations, notify the provider and surgeon - options that proceed or persuade violate autonomy.
nx_moc_006: DNR limits resuscitation only: comfort care continues fully - treat the dyspnea and anxiety aggressively. Options that withhold palliative measures misread the order.
nx_moc_007: Overheard PHI in a public space is a confidentiality breach: address it directly with the colleagues and report per policy. Ignoring or joining the conversation compounds it.
nx_moc_008: Floating rules: accept the assignment, take the tasks you are competent for, and negotiate unfamiliar specialty tasks to qualified staff - flat refusal is abandonment, silent acceptance is unsafe.
nx_moc_009: Disaster triage inverts everyday priority: treat first the IMMEDIATE category - life-threatening but survivable with quick intervention. The most critically injured beyond saving are expectant, not first.
nx_moc_010: Delegation SATA: run each option through the same filter - stable client, routine task, no judgment required. Accept all that pass; one assessment word fails an option.
nx_moc_011: After a med error with a stable client: notify the provider, monitor, document the facts in the chart, and complete the incident report - the trap options either hide the error or chart the report.
nx_moc_012: Two clients, one nurse: gurgling from a fresh tracheostomy is an airway threat and wins over anything non-airway - answer with who you go to first, then how you get help to the other.
nx_moc_013: Choking on thin liquids after stroke points to the swallowing specialist: speech-language pathology owns dysphagia evaluation - dietitian and PT options are adjacent-role decoys.
nx_moc_014: Valid consent SATA: capacity, voluntariness, and disclosure of procedure, risks, benefits and alternatives. Options about family agreement or witness counts are not elements.
nx_pad_001: Read ABGs in two steps: pH 7.30 is acidotic, CO2 58 is the respiratory culprit; then check HCO3 for compensation. Name the primary disorder before touching the options.
nx_pad_002: Twenty minutes of hyperventilation with perioral numbness is respiratory alkalosis blowing off CO2: the intervention is slow, coached breathing - the old paper-bag options are unsafe distractors.
nx_pad_003: Potassium 6.8 on the ECG: peaked (tented) T waves come first - the answer pairing the highest K with the earliest classic change.
nx_pad_004: Perioral and finger tingling after thyroidectomy is hypocalcemia from parathyroid injury: confirm with Chvostek/Trousseau and have calcium gluconate ready - the timeline plus location is the fingerprint.
nx_pad_005: Wheeze, facial swelling and hypotension minutes into a new drug is anaphylaxis: stop the infusion FIRST, then epinephrine per protocol, airway, fluids - sequence options test whether you stop the trigger.
nx_pad_006: Pounding headache with flushing above a T6 lesion is autonomic dysreflexia: sit the client upright, then hunt the trigger - a blocked catheter or full bladder - before medicating pressure.
nx_pad_007: Pain out of proportion, worse on passive stretch, in a casted limb is compartment syndrome: this is a report-immediately answer - elevating and icing options worsen perfusion.
nx_pad_008: Jaw rigidity with soaring end-tidal CO2 under anesthesia is malignant hyperthermia: the paired answer is dantrolene and stop the triggering agent - temperature rise is a late sign, so do not wait for fever options.
nx_pad_009: Suction technique: preoxygenate, apply suction only WHILE WITHDRAWING, limit passes to about 10 seconds. Options suctioning during insertion or prolonging passes trade oxygen for secretions.
nx_pad_010: DKA expected-findings SATA: Kussmaul respirations, fruity breath, dehydration signs, glucose high with pH low. Reject findings of the opposite disorder (HHS's absent ketones) or fluid overload.
nx_pad_011: Fluid-excess SATA reads the volume exam: crackles, S3, JVD, dependent edema, rapid weight gain. Reject the dehydration set - poor turgor, orthostatics, concentrated urine.
nx_pad_012: 3% saline is a correct-slowly drug: infuse via pump at low rates with frequent sodium checks - overcorrection injures the brain, so the consideration option about rate and monitoring wins.
nx_pht_001: Nausea, anorexia and yellow-halo vision on digoxin is toxicity: hold the dose, check the level and potassium, notify - visual changes are the exam's favourite digoxin flag.
nx_pht_002: NPH is intermediate-acting: peak lands mid-afternoon after a morning dose, so watch for hypoglycemia roughly 4 to 12 hours later - match the insulin's peak window, not its onset.
nx_pht_003: Warfarin is monitored by INR with a usual therapeutic range near 2 to 3: the option quoting aPTT belongs to heparin - matching drug to lab is the entire question.
nx_pht_004: Heparin's antidote is protamine sulfate: reversal questions are matching questions, and vitamin K options belong to warfarin.
nx_pht_005: Before IV morphine, respiratory rate rules: a low rate (or deep sedation) holds the dose - the finding that depresses breathing outranks pain scores in a hold-the-drug frame.
nx_pht_006: Acetaminophen overdose antidote is N-acetylcysteine: given on the nomogram schedule to protect the liver - naloxone and flumazenil options are wrong-receptor decoys.
nx_pht_007: Rapid flushing during vancomycin is an infusion-rate reaction: slow or pause the infusion per protocol - it is rate-related histamine release, and 'stop drug forever' options overshoot.
nx_pht_008: ACE-inhibitor teaching: avoid potassium supplements and salt substitutes (potassium chloride) - the hyperkalemia interaction is the tested pairing; the dry cough is a report-not-avoid item.
nx_pht_009: Lithium follows sodium and water: low-sodium diet plus sweating concentrates the drug toward toxicity - the teaching answer maintains consistent sodium and hydration and knows the early toxicity signs.
nx_pht_010: Insulin's high-alert safeguard is independent double-checking and using insulin-specific syringes: the option naming a second-nurse verification is the specific practice; general five-rights options are too generic.
nx_pht_011: Feeling unwell 90 minutes after rapid-acting insulin is peak-time hypoglycemia: check the glucose and treat with fast carbohydrate - the timing is the diagnostic clue.
nx_pht_012: Digoxin hold-the-dose SATA: apical pulse below 60, toxicity symptoms, potassium abnormalities, elevated level. Each option is a gate; any single failed gate holds the drug.
nx_psy_001: Fear stems reward reflection first: acknowledge and open the feeling ('This is frightening - tell me more'). Reassurance, false cheerfulness and 'why' questions are the standard wrong answers.
nx_psy_002: 'Better off without me' is a cue, and the answer is a direct suicide inquiry: ask plainly about thoughts of self-harm - directness does not plant ideas, and deflection options fail safety.
nx_psy_003: Stated intent plus a specific plan is the highest risk tier: one-to-one observation and a safe environment now - contract-for-safety options are recognised distractors.
nx_psy_004: A pint daily plus tremors and agitation at 48 hours is alcohol withdrawal heading toward DTs: anticipate the protocol (benzodiazepines, monitoring) - treating it as anxiety misses the timeline.
nx_psy_005: Bruises in varied healing stages plus an inconsistent story is a mandated report: nurses report suspicion, not proof - options that investigate privately or wait for certainty are wrong in law.
nx_psy_006: IPV screening happens alone, in private, with direct nonjudgmental questions - any option that includes the partner in the interview invalidates it.
nx_psy_007: Hearing the deceased's voice two weeks out is within normal grief: normalise and support - options that pathologise it or refer for antipsychotics misgrade normal bereavement.
nx_psy_008: Panic-attack response: stay physically present, short simple sentences, slow the breathing with them - teaching and exploring options belong AFTER the attack, not during.
nx_psy_009: In dementia, redirect rather than confront: enter the feeling ('Tell me about your work') and steer to an activity - reality-orientation options escalate; lying outright is also wrong. Validation plus redirection wins.
nx_psy_010: Therapeutic-technique SATA: accept open-ended questions, reflection, silence, offering self; reject 'why' questions, false reassurance, advice and approval - four therapeutic, four blocked, sort accordingly.
nx_rrp_001: Potassium 2.8 acts on two fronts: hold anything that lowers it further (and any digoxin), and notify for replacement - but the PRIORITY option is the safety hold-and-report, not documentation.
nx_rrp_002: Sodium 118 with confusion is seizure territory: institute seizure precautions while correction proceeds - the precaution answer beats the recheck-the-lab answer at this depth.
nx_rrp_003: Unsigned consent plus premedication: the sedative invalidates capacity, so surgery waits - notify and hold. Options obtaining the signature now are the legal trap.
nx_rrp_004: Low-grade fever with diminished breath sounds 36 hours post-op is atelectasis: the answer is lung expansion - incentive spirometry, ambulation, cough and deep breathe - not antibiotics yet.
nx_rrp_005: Chest-drain chambers: gentle intermittent water-seal bubbling is normal, CONTINUOUS vigorous bubbling means an air leak - locate and report; clamping options endanger the client.
nx_rrp_006: The single best CAUTI prevention is removing the catheter as soon as possible: daily necessity review beats any cleaning-technique option in a 'best' frame.
nx_rrp_007: NPO diabetic on insulin: clarify the insulin order with the provider - the trap options either give the full dose fasting or hold everything without asking.
nx_rrp_008: Post-femoral-catheterization assessment is a paired check: puncture site for bleeding AND distal pulses for perfusion, with the leg straight - options with only one half of the pair are incomplete.
nx_rrp_009: Platelets 38,000 is bleeding-precaution teaching: soft toothbrush, electric razor, no aspirin/NSAIDs, avoid invasive procedures - infection-precaution options belong to the neutropenia question.
nx_rrp_010: INR 5.4 without bleeding: hold warfarin and notify - vitamin K only per order and protocol. The extremes (continue the dose; give FFP now) bracket the measured correct action.
nx_rrp_011: DVT-prevention SATA: early ambulation, calf exercises, compression devices, prescribed prophylaxis. Reject knee-pillow and prolonged-sitting options - anything that kinks venous return.
nx_rrp_012: Critical-value triage: report immediately the values that kill soon - potassium extremes, sodium extremes, critical glucose, INR far out of range - and let mildly abnormal chronic values wait for rounds.
nx_sic_001: Measles is airborne: negative-pressure room plus N95 respirator - the strictest category on offer. Mixing droplet equipment with airborne disease is the planted error.
nx_sic_002: Meningococcal meningitis needs droplet precautions until 24 hours of effective antibiotics: at 6 hours the mask stays on - options lifting precautions early miss the 24-hour rule.
nx_sic_003: C. difficile hands demand soap and water - alcohol gel does not kill spores. The mechanism (spores) is the reason and the answer.
nx_sic_004: Donning order: gown, mask, eyewear, gloves - clean to dirty, gloves last so they cover the gown cuffs. Doffing reverses with gloves first.
nx_sic_005: Doffing starts with the dirtiest item: gloves come off FIRST, then eyewear, gown, mask - the sequence protects your face from your own contaminated hands.
nx_sic_006: Restraints after alternatives fail: provider order within the required window, correct tie (quick-release to the frame, never rails), scheduled circulation and needs checks - the option bundling order-plus-monitoring is correct.
nx_sic_007: Fall-risk interventions are proximity and environment: bed low and locked, call bell in reach, nonskid footwear, frequent rounding - restraint and full-rails options increase injury and are wrong.
nx_sic_008: Fire response is RACE and the R is rescue: remove the client from immediate danger first, then alarm, confine, extinguish - options that fight the fire first invert the acronym.
nx_sic_009: C. difficile SATA: contact precautions, dedicated equipment, soap-and-water hands, sporicidal cleaning. Reject alcohol-gel and 'standard precautions suffice' options - spores drive every correct choice.
nx_sic_010: Home-oxygen 'needs further teaching' hunts the unsafe statement: anything tolerating smoking, open flames, or petroleum products near oxygen is the answer - you are selecting the error, not the truth.
nx_sic_011: Needlestick prevention after injection: never recap - activate the safety device and drop it in the sharps container immediately. Recapping options are the classic planted error.
nx_sic_012: Seizure-room SATA: suction and oxygen at bedside, padded rails per policy, IV access, bed low. Reject the two dangerous folk answers - tongue blades and restraining the client mid-seizure.
